analysis.title: Weekly Headings Snapshot (Week Ending November 6, 2026)
key_insights: Following the midterm results, the report highlights five of the biggest questions ahead for the economy and markets.
Despite post-midterm volatility, history suggests congressional turnover is not a headwind for equities.
The US economy added 165,000 jobs in October and the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%.
The 10-year Treasury yield has fallen 48 bps from its 5.31% peak one month ago to its lowest level since Labor Day.
Democrats secured control of both the House (about 240 seats, the figure is garbled in the source) and the Senate (currently 54 seats) in the midterm elections.
More than 10 Fed officials are scheduled to speak next week, and their remarks could offer clues on the rate path ahead of the December FOMC meeting.
CPI is released Tuesday 11/10 and PPI on Friday 11/13. The report expects headline CPI to stay at +3.7% and core CPI at +2.6% YoY.
The NFIB Small Business Index on Tuesday will help gauge the outlook for small businesses, which make up about 40% of US economic activity. Price metrics and employment are the components to watch.

Weekly performance (Thursday close to Thursday close): S&P 500 -4.7%, Russell MidCap -3.5%, Russell 2000 -4.5%, AC World -3.5%, Emerging Markets -3.0%, BG Commodity -4.5%, US Dollar -0.5%, US Aggregate Bond +0.8%.
